themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Most of these problems have no answer key. There is no stable number to grade your work against, and the thing you are measuring often shifts while you measure it, so the models start by building a small truth set of their own or admit the number is only an estimate.
themes.evidence: On answer engine optimization all three models say the output is non-deterministic and drifts more than any action they take; on cross-channel incrementality the platform reacts to the test itself; on identity resolution Claude recruits a consenting panel because no one knows who is really the same person; on content review the models say expert reviewers disagree, so there is nothing stable to automate toward.

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Many of these problems stall because the people holding the answer gain nothing by sharing it, and nobody can force them. The blockers are money and politics, inside the company as much as outside, so the models try to make honesty or cooperation pay rather than write another rule.
themes.evidence: On agentic traffic all three models build a fast lane with better prices or cleaner data so declaring beats spoofing; on journey orchestration the blocker is channel owners paid on their own numbers; on the semantic context layer the models call conflicting definitions a political settlement, not a modeling gap; on ad supply integrity Gemini says the market profits from fake volume.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what happens next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email, a spent dollar, or an exported file cannot be taken back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: On safe agent execution every model puts a proxy or gateway in front of every write with hard spend, rate, and audience caps because sends and spend cannot be rolled back; on downstream consent the models route all data exits through a single checkpoint and switch to daily expiring audiences; on journey orchestration they build one shared contact log that every channel must check before sending.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, a message, or a dollar leaves your own systems, you cannot see inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. You can watch from outside and guess whether the rules were followed, but you cannot prove it.
themes.evidence: On downstream consent all three models say black-box ad platforms and already-trained models offer no person-level proof of deletion, leaving canary tests as the honest ceiling; on incrementality the platforms control both the treatment and the evidence; on agent execution vendors expose neither agent identity nor rollback; on ad supply integrity the chain of impressions can be fabricated at many points.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls turn on meaning and context: whether a picture plus a headline implies a promise, whether evidence really backs a claim, whether two teams can both be right about what a word means. No rule set captures that, so the models shrink human judgment into a smaller, safer box instead of removing it.
themes.evidence: On generative content governance today all three models build a registry of pre-approved claims and restrict generation to it, while agreeing the implied claim created by tone or an image beside a headline is exactly what software cannot judge; on the semantic context layer the models say a single definition of customer is the wrong target and only forced disclosure of which definition was used can work.
